name: Musaddad ibn Musarhad
nameAr: مسدد بن مسرهد بن مسربل بن مستورد الأسدي البصري

laqab.en: 'Musaddad' is said to be a laqab: his name is also given as Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz (Taqrib)

bornNote: About 150 AH, as the Shamela record estimates; no early source fetched gives a year.
diedNote: 228 AH (al-Bukhari and others); Ibn Qani': at the start of Ramadan.

taqrib.ar: ثقة حافظ، يقال إنه أول من صنف المسند بالبصرة، من العاشرة، مات سنة ثمان وعشرين، ويقال اسمه عبد الملك بن عبد العزيز ومسدد لقب
taqrib.en: Reliable, a hadith master; said to be the first to compile a Musnad in Basra; of the tenth generation; died in 228. It is said his name was Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz and Musaddad a laqab.

role: Teacher of al-Bukhari and Abu Dawud; said to be the first Basran to compile a Musnad

teachers.name: Abdullah ibn Yahya ibn Abi Kathir
teachers.nameAr: عبد الله بن يحيى بن أبي كثير

verdicts.via: Ja'far ibn Abi Uthman, who asked him from whom to write in Basra
verdicts.ar: اكتب عن مسدد فإنه ثقة ثقة
verdicts.en: Write from Musaddad, for he is reliable, reliable.
verdicts.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, letter mim, entry 203; Tahdhib al-Kamal 27/443

verdicts.ar: مسدد صدوق، فما كتبت عنه فلا تعده
verdicts.en: Musaddad is truthful; whatever you wrote from him, do not go back over it.
verdicts.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, letter mim, entry 203; al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 8/438

verdicts.ar: لو أتيت مسددا فحدثته في بيته لكان يستأهل
verdicts.en: If I went to Musaddad and narrated to him in his own house, he would deserve it.
verdicts.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, letter mim, entry 203; al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 8/438

verdicts.ar: مسدد بن مسرهد بن مسربل بن مستورد الأسدي البصري ثقة، كان يملي علي حتى أضجر
verdicts.en: Musaddad ibn Musarhad ibn Musarbal ibn Mustawrid al-Asadi al-Basri is reliable; he would dictate to me until I grew weary.

verdicts.via: Abu Amr ibn Hakim, on Musaddad's hadith from Yahya ibn Sa'id from Ubaydullah from Nafi' from Ibn Umar
verdicts.ar: كأنها الدنانير، ثم قال: كأنك سمعتها من في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
verdicts.en: They are like gold dinars; then he said: as if you heard them from the Prophet's own mouth.

verdicts.ar: يقال إنه أول من صنف المسند بالبصرة
verdicts.en: It is said he was the first to compile a Musnad in Basra.

flags.label: A lineage like a charm
flags.detail: Al-Ijli reports that Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn would ask him to recite Musaddad's genealogy (Musaddad ibn Musarhad ibn Musarbal ibn Mustawrid) and say: 'Ahmad, this is a charm against the scorpion's sting.' Al-Bukhari named the great-grandfather Mar'abal; Ibn Hajar rejects Mansur al-Khalidi's far longer version as unsupported.

flags.label: Not used by Muslim or Ibn Majah
flags.detail: His sigla are خ د ت س: al-Bukhari and Abu Dawud heard from him directly; al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i reach him through intermediaries (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib). Muslim and Ibn Majah do not narrate from him.

bio: A Basran hadith master, one of al-Bukhari's and Abu Dawud's shaykhs, said to be the first in Basra to arrange hadith as a Musnad. Ibn Ma'in, al-Nasa'i, Abu Hatim, al-Ijli and Ibn Qani' call him reliable, and Ibn Ma'in told a student that he was the man to write from in Basra. Ahmad's 'truthful' sits beside these. He died in 228.

provenance.field: nameAr, kunya, laqab, tabaqa, taqrib, died, rumuz
